title: Char Siu Pork
subtitle: Chinese barbecue pork with honey and five-spice
excerpt: Char siu is Cantonese barbecue pork with a sticky, lacquered coating of soy, honey and five-spice. The marinade caramelises beautifully in a hot oven to give deep colour and sweet-savoury flavour. Serve over steamed rice or shred through noodles.
sourceNotes: Char siu is one of the most iconic dishes in Cantonese cuisine, historically cooked in wood-fired ovens. The name translates literally as 'fork roasted', referring to the long forks used to hold the meat over the fire.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the cooked, cooled pork for up to 2 months. Reheat in a hot oven for 10 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Scales easily. Marinate and roast in batches.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate overnight in the fridge for the best colour and flavour.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 180C / Gas 6. Increase to 220C for the final 5 minutes to caramelise the glaze.

content.text: Slice the pork shoulder into strips about 2cm thick so the marinade penetrates all the way through. The longer you leave it marinating, the better the colour and the more intense the flavour.
Mix together the honey, light soy, dark soy, mirin, five-spice, garlic and ginger in a bowl. Add the pork strips and turn to coat. Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Heat the oven to 200C (fan 180C / gas 6). Place a wire rack over a foil-lined roasting tin. Lift the pork strips from the marinade, shaking off the excess, and lay on the rack. Reserve the marinade.
Roast for 15 minutes. Brush with the reserved marinade, flip and roast for another 10 minutes.
Raise the oven to 220C (fan 200C). Brush with marinade once more and roast for a final 5 to 8 minutes until the surface is caramelised and sticky.
Leave to rest for 10 minutes before slicing across the grain and serving.

items.symptom: Pork is pale with no caramelisation
items.cause: Oven not hot enough for the final blast.
items.fix: Raise the heat and brush with extra honey and soy.

items.symptom: Glaze burned before pork cooked through
items.cause: Too much sugar in the marinade or strips too thick.
items.fix: Cover with foil and finish cooking at lower heat.
